subject: Deployment path & capacity priorities — dedicated + VPC clarifications
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@neptune.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Quick follow-up + traffic profile

Thanks for the call earlier — great to meet the team. Attached is the traffic CSV I mentioned (neptune_traffic_profile.csv) showing a two-week snapshot and the current mix of requests. A couple quick notes from our side: we have a bursty pattern tied to business hours in PST, ~200–300 TPS peak for inference endpoints, and three main payload shapes: short search/complete (avg ~20 tokens), chat-like multi-turn prompts (avg ~120 tokens), and a small fraction (~3–6%) of long-context extraction requests where clients upload ~2k tokens. Latency targets are important — our product team wants 95th percentile under 150 ms end-to-end for the short/medium requests.

Two asks from procurement: can you share a rough order-of-magnitude on committed capacity pricing for a Dedicated pool vs initial Hosted run? Also, can you call out what pieces would require a VPC vs on-prem for compliance? Looping in procurement at procurement@neptune.ai.

Appreciate the recap, Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Product, Neptune Analytics

Attachments: neptune_traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 45 KB)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@neptune.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + traffic profile

Sam — thanks for the data and for the call. High-level takeaways and questions below so we can size a dedicated pool and surface trade-offs versus Hosted / Private VPC: 

- Traffic shape: 200–300 TPS peak aligns with a mid-sized dedicated pool. We’ll want a 2–3x safety buffer for bursts and autoscaling granularity — practical target for initial reserved throughput: ~600 TPS sustained headroom.
- Token mix: short (20t) and medium (120t) prompts are mostly latency-sensitive; long-context jobs (2k tokens) will drive memory pressure (KV cache) and might be best routed to a different model variant or pre-warmed workers.
- Concurrency: for latency SLOs I’d start with 12–16 concurrent streams per GPU for an A100-class node if quantized; H100 can push higher but is more expensive. If you want tighter 95p latency (<=120 ms), we should bias to fewer concurrent streams and faster GPUs.
- GPU recommendation options:
  * Cost-first: A100-80GB (x2 nodes) — good balance for mixed token mixes with batching and KV cache tuning.
  * Latency-first: H100-80GB (x1–2 nodes) — better 95p tail but higher unit cost.
- VPC vs on-prem: VPC (private link) will satisfy most compliance needs and keeps control plane in Redwood while isolating network. On-prem only necessary if you require full air-gap or local data residency.

I’ve attached a short worksheet and will coordinate an ops/architecture sync to pick the exact GPU mix + autoscale policy. Can you confirm: target 95p latency goal (is 150 ms acceptable or do you need <=120 ms?), and an answer on whether you require VPC or on-prem? Also, who from procurement should I include for pricing?

Next step: I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical sizing call with Neha (engineer) and Vanessa (CS lead) — suggested times below.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sizing-worksheet.xlsx (XLSX, stub)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@neptune.ai>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + traffic profile — technical notes

Adding a few technical specifics to help your infra team evaluate options: 

- Batching & queueing: For mixed token sizes we recommend dynamic batching with per-model max_batch_size=64 and token-length-aware batching windows (short-medium separate from 2k jobs). This reduces per-token cost while keeping tail latency reasonable.
- KV cache sizing: long-context jobs will require reserved KV capacity on workers or offload to larger GPUs. If you route the 2k requests to a slipstreamed worker class (H100 preferred), you avoid blowing up latency on short requests.
- Concurrent streams: empirically we see ~14 concurrent short-streams per A100 with quantized weights for 95p under 150ms when the model is LLAMA-like. For LLMs with bigger context or larger parameter counts, drop to 8–10 streams or choose H100.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: recommend policy to fallback to a cheaper host-model (quantized) when capacity constrained, and to return a concise degraded response with an explicit header so clients can adapt.

I’ll put together a brief sizing PDF (redwood-dedicated-sizing-summary.pdf) that maps your sample CSV to GPU families, estimated nodes, and monthly committed spend ranges for 3 commitment tiers. We’ll bring that to the technical sizing call.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-summary.pdf (PDF, stub)

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@neptune.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@neptune.ai>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment path & capacity priorities — dedicated + VPC clarifications

Thanks Marcus / Neha — that all makes sense and aligns with internal thinking. A few clarifications so procurement/infrastructure can move forward: 

- We’re leaning toward Dedicated pool with VPC peering (not full on-prem) — primary reason: data residency in our cloud account and we want private networking.
- Target TPS: realistic sustained baseline ~150 TPS, 95p peaks ~280 TPS. We need to support peaks with an autoscale buffer so customer-facing SLAs are met.
- Latency: short/medium requests need 95p <= 120 ms if possible. If that forces H100 choices for the hot pool, we’re open to the delta in price — we just want clear trade-offs.
- Token distribution: ~70% short (<32t), 25% medium (32–256t), 5% long (>1024t). The long jobs are offline-ish and can be routed to a lower-priority pool.

Procurement contact is procurement@neptune.ai — please include an initial committed pricing estimate for 3 tiers (12-month commit, 6-month pilot, and pay-as-you-go) and call out any minimums for Dedicated. Also confirm expected lead times for Dedicated pool provisioning (VM/GPU reservation + VPC setup).

We’re available for the technical sizing call Tuesday or Wednesday PST.

—Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Product, Neptune Analytics

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@neptune.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Procurement <procurement@neptune.ai>

Sam — perfect, that gives us everything we need for the next step. Quick plan / immediate asks: 

1) I’ll send a 30-minute invite for tomorrow (Tuesday) 10:00 PST with Neha and Vanessa to walk the sizing PDF and lock the GPU mix.
2) Neha & I will produce a three-tier committed-pricing sketch (12m commit / 6m pilot / PAYG) and include provisioning lead-times (we typically see 5–12 business days for Dedicated pools depending on GPU availability + VPC networking setup).
3) Action for Neptune: confirm whether long-context jobs must remain in the same VPC (we recommend routing long jobs to a separate lower-priority pool to avoid tail impacts).

Deliverables we’ll share before the call: redwood-dedicated-sizing-summary.pdf, a one-pager that maps latency vs cost for A100 vs H100, and a proposed autoscale policy (min nodes, burst headroom, cooldown).

If that sounds good I’ll lock the calendar and get procurement the pricing sheet.

Thanks — talk tomorrow,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
